title: Tough feedback
tagline: Learn to address repeated missed deadlines with clear evidence, diagnose the root cause, and agree on a concrete recovery plan.
setting: Conversations happen in a private meeting room or video call, scheduled or ad-hoc, after a deadline has been missed or is at risk.

scenarios.label: First missed deadline
scenarios.desc: Address a single missed milestone with a usually reliable contributor.
scenarios.setup: The team member sits down looking tense. They open with: “I know the prototype didn’t ship Friday. I’ve got the logs if you want them.”
scenarios.objective: Agree on what specifically was missed and capture their perspective on why.
scenarios.moment: Monday 9:15 am, coffee cooling on the table

scenarios.label: Pattern of missed deadlines
scenarios.desc: Confront a recurring pattern across three sprints with a senior engineer.
scenarios.setup: The engineer leans back, arms folded. They open with: “Which one this time? The API freeze, the docs, or the demo?”
scenarios.objective: Identify the systemic root cause, planning, scope, dependencies, or capacity, and commit to one process change.

scenarios.label: Recovery plan commitment
scenarios.desc: Lock in a concrete, measurable recovery plan with a member who agrees there’s a problem but resists oversight.
scenarios.setup: The team member nods slowly. They open with: “Okay, I hear you. I’ll just work weekends and catch up, no need for extra process.”
scenarios.objective: Replace vague promises with a written plan: scoped work, intermediate checkpoints, and a shared tracking method.

buyers.angle: Believes deadlines are flexible if work is thorough.
Calls missed deadline a miscommunication not negligence.
Threatens to quit if feedback changes.
Wants data proof before adjusting schedule.

objections: I was waiting on resources that arrived late
The scope changed mid‑sprint and I had to adjust
I thought the deadline was flexible given the quality
I got pulled into an emergency that took priority
I didn’t understand the deadline was firm
My previous projects always had buffer time
I was testing a new approach that required extra time
No one told me the deadline was critical

rubric.label: Specific evidence
rubric.what: Opens with the exact missed commitment, date, and impact, no vague language or hearsay.

rubric.label: Curious diagnosis
rubric.what: Asks open ‘what’ questions to uncover planning gaps, unclear scope, or dependency blockers before offering solutions.

rubric.label: Impact clarity
rubric.what: Explains how the miss affected the project, stakeholders, or teammates without blame or exaggeration.

rubric.label: Realistic recommitment
rubric.what: Co-creates a recovery plan with scoped work, buffer, and intermediate checkpoints grounded in past velocity.

rubric.label: Feedback loop design
rubric.what: Proposes a shorter, structured cadence, stand-ups, demo checkpoints, or async updates, to catch drift early.

rubric.label: Fairness consistency
rubric.what: Applies the same standard and process used with other team members; documents the conversation per policy.

pitfalls: Softening the message with sandwich feedback and losing the concrete ask.
Accepting ‘I’ll work harder’ without a written plan and checkpoints.
Skipping documentation required by HR or performance policy.
line: Giving tough feedback to a team member who keeps missing deadlines

research.text: When giving tough feedback to a team member who keeps missing deadlines, it's important to start by precisely stating the missed deadline and asking what happened, avoiding generalizations. Sources suggest exploring potential reasons such as poor planning skills or unclear expectations. It's advised to have an uncomfortable conversation, framing feedback constructively, and emphasizing the importance of meeting deadlines for the overall project success. If it's a pattern, diagnose the root cause by asking "what" questions instead of judgmental ones. Sources also recommend making deadlines realistic, using evidence from similar work, and creating shorter feedback loops to correct problems before deadlines are missed.
